Ground Ops

Servicios en tierra

All services required by an aircraft between landing and take-off, excluding air traffic control services. This includes baggage handling, refueling, catering, and aircraft marshaling.

Quick answer: All services required by an aircraft between landing and take-off, excluding air traffic control services. This includes baggage handling, refueling, catering, and aircraft marshaling.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Servicios en tierra?

In this glossary, Servicios en tierra refers to: All services required by an aircraft between landing and take-off, excluding air traffic control services. This includes baggage handling, refueling, catering, and aircraft marshaling.

How is Servicios en tierra used in aviation?

In aviation communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Solicito confirmación de que los servicios en tierra están organizados para la llegada a la puerta B12."

Why does Servicios en tierra matter in aviation?

Servicios en tierra matters because it supports clear communication in Ground Ops contexts for Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as ICAO Level 4, ICAO Level 5, ICAO Level 6, and EASA FCL.055.

Servicios en tierra is mainly used by Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew.
